lines.name: Pennsylvania Avenue line (Georgetown–Navy Yard)
lines.streets: M St NW (Georgetown) – Pennsylvania Ave NW/SE – Navy Yard; extended 1895 from 32nd St to 36th & M St (Georgetown Car Barn); extended on Pennsylvania Ave SE from 8th St to 17th St SE in 1901, later to Barney Circle
lines.later: Capital Traction (1895); Capital Transit (1933); D.C. Transit (1956)
lines.power: Horse → cable (1892) → horse again after Sept 1897 powerhouse fire → underground conduit electric (1898)
lines.routes: 30 (Wisconsin Ave–Pennsylvania Ave SE); 54 (14th St–Pennsylvania Ave to Navy Yard)
lines.notes: Capitol–White House July 29, 1862; Washington Circle Aug 12; Georgetown Aug 18; Navy Yard Oct 2. Electrified Apr 20, 1898. West End loop 1901. West End loops: see L56. Map: westbound cars used a Wisconsin Ave, Prospect St and 34th St loop in 1946 (Tundria), and the line used M St and 26th St between 1875 and 1916 (1880 map). 1912 map (audit): the 1901 extension ended in a loop around the block at 15th St SE.

lines.name: 7th Street line
lines.streets: 7th St NW/SW from Boundary St (Florida Ave) to the Potomac wharves; extended to the Arsenal (Fort McNair) in 1875; ran along M St SW to 7th St
lines.later: Capital Traction (1895); Capital Transit; D.C. Transit
lines.power: Horse → cable (May 12, 1890, DC's first cable line) → horse after 1897 fire → electric conduit (1898)
lines.notes: Opened Nov 15, 1862. DC's first cable line (Apr 12, 1890 per Wikipedia; May 12 per NRHP). Electrified May 26, 1898. Cable powerhouse at P & Water Sts SW. 1912 map: south of M St the line ran along the old Water St beside the Washington Channel to P St and the Arsenal gate (the modern Maine Ave and Wharf streets are drawn differently, so this stretch is drawn straight).

lines.name: 14th Street line
lines.streets: 14th St NW from Boundary St to the Treasury (15th St & New York Ave); extended up the hill to Park Rd (Mount Pleasant) c.1892–95; extended to Colorado Ave 1906–07 (Decatur St car barn); Colorado Ave terminal by 1937
lines.later: Capital Traction (1895); Capital Transit; D.C. Transit
lines.power: Horse → cable (1892; CRF lists 1895) → electric conduit (1898)
lines.notes: Electrified Feb 27, 1898. First PCC cars Aug 1937. Last scheduled run left 14th & Colorado 2:17 am, Jan 28, 1962.

lines.name: Georgetown–B&O Depot (Capitol Hill) line
lines.streets: Georgetown to the B&O depot at New Jersey Ave & C St NW; later Mount Pleasant–B&O Depot via Pennsylvania Ave and 14th St (cable era)
lines.endtxt: Absorbed into other routes (depot razed after 1907)
lines.notes: One of four W&G services in 1863 (21 cars).

lines.name: Metropolitan main line (Capitol–War Dept; later F St/D St line)
lines.streets: Charter route (1864): A St & New Jersey Ave via D, C, Indiana Ave, 5th, F and 14th Sts. As built (Jan 1865): Capitol to 14th & I Sts NW, plus H St NW from Massachusetts Ave to 17th St
lines.later: Washington Traction & Electric (1899); WRECo (1902); Capital Transit; D.C. Transit
lines.notes: CRF dates horse service 1865. 1912 map: a link ran along Indiana Ave from D St to C St at 1st St NW.

lines.name: 9th Street line
lines.streets: 9th St NW north from M St to Boundary St, joining the Boundary & Silver Spring line
lines.power: Horse (1872) → first underground-conduit electric line in DC (1895)
lines.notes: Sources disagree on the conversion year: NRHP says 1933 with the rebuilding of 9th St; Ghosts of DC says cars were pulled in 1936. Map: 9th St track continued south to Pennsylvania Ave (1912 map); route 40 ran via 9th St, Pennsylvania Ave and C St NW in 1946. 1912 map: north of Florida Ave the 9th St track curved northwest to join the 11th St line near Kenyon St (date of this curve not documented).

lines.name: P Street / Georgetown line
lines.streets: P St NW west from Dupont Circle to Georgetown (36th & Prospect St), built under the Union Railroad charter; completed 1880
lines.notes: Union RR absorbed Aug–Nov 1872 without authority. Georgetown loop on P, 36th, Prospect and 35th Sts authorized 1895. Rails remain on O & P Sts between 33rd and 35th Sts NW. Map: the Georgetown P and O St loop west of Wisconsin Ave stayed in use for Cabin John cars until 1960 (1958 trackage map). 1912 map: a loop east of Wisconsin Ave ran via P St, 28th St and Dumbarton St. 1912 map (Georgetown): cars ran out P St to 36th St, down to the car barn at Prospect St, along Prospect and up 35th St, then east on O St across Wisconsin Ave into Dumbarton St and back up 28th St. The original 1873 loop used P, 35th, O and 33rd Sts; the O St and P St loop west of Wisconsin was later the Cabin John cars' terminal (1935–60, from the 1958 trackage map).

lines.name: 4th Street NW/SW line
lines.streets: 4½ St (now 4th St) SW from Missouri Ave to P St SW / Arsenal; reached via unauthorized tracks on B St, 6th St and Missouri Ave
lines.notes: CRF gives '1930s' only; end year approximate. Map: reached 4½ St via 9th St, B St (Constitution Ave), 6th St and Missouri Ave (1880 and 1912 maps). 1912 map: 4½ St is today's 4th St SW; the line ran down Missouri Ave from 6th & B Sts onto it. In service 1940 per DC PUC Order No. 1902 (July 17, 1940), which still routes 4th St SW/P St SW (Arsenal) trackage; abandoned by 1946. End year is approximate.

lines.name: East Capitol Street line
lines.streets: East Capitol St to 9th St (by 1888); extended 1896 to the East Capitol St car barn / Lincoln Park loop (1400 East Capitol St)
lines.notes: One of the last two car barns in service (Lincoln Park). Map: reached East Capitol St via C St, Delaware Ave, B St (Constitution Ave) and 1st St NE (1880 map). 1912 map: tracks ran around both sides of Lincoln Park and ended in a loop around the block east of the park.

lines.name: Connecticut Avenue line (south)
lines.streets: Connecticut Ave from 17th St & New York Ave / White House north to Boundary St (Florida Ave)
lines.later: Metropolitan (1874); WRECo; Capital Transit; D.C. Transit
lines.notes: Horsecars ran only to P St in 1873; the track north to Florida Ave was paved over and then revived as a shuttle in 1883. Dupont Circle underpass opened Nov 2, 1949. Conflict: the 1880 statistical map shows track on Connecticut Ave to S St, although Tindall and Wikipedia say the section north of P St was paved over until 1883. 1912 map: the line ran on 17th St between H St and K St, joining Connecticut Ave at Farragut Square.

lines.name: Mount Pleasant extension
lines.streets: Columbia Rd from Connecticut & Florida Aves to 18th St (1897), then Columbia Rd east to 'old Sixteenth St' (today's Mount Pleasant St) and north to Park St (1900)
lines.notes: Authorized Feb 27, 1897; service began June 6, 1900 (the earlier 1896 date was wrong).

lines.name: Georgia Avenue (7th St Extended / Brightwood) line
lines.streets: Georgia Ave (Brightwood Ave) from Florida Ave to Rock Creek Church Rd (horse, 1873), then to Brightwood and the Silver Spring district line
lines.co: Boundary & Silver Spring Railway (chartered 1872; bought by Metropolitan Dec 1872)
lines.later: Brightwood Railway (1888/1890); WRECo; Capital Transit; D.C. Transit
lines.power: Horse → Judson pneumatic trial (1889–90, failed) → overhead electric ordered 1892 → underground conduit ordered 1898
lines.notes: CRF gives electric 1890; Wikipedia says Congress ordered overhead electric in 1892. The 1880 map (and Berman's 2019 redraw) labels the city end of this line 'Pleasant Plains', possibly because the map stops at the city limit. Electrified by 1892–93: Congress ordered overhead trolley by act of July 26, 1892, and the line was electric by 1893 (CRF's "1890" reflects the 1889–90 Judson pneumatic trial).

lines.name: Takoma branch (Brightwood Railway)
lines.streets: Georgia Ave to Butternut St (then Umatilla St) and 4th St NW, Takoma Park

lines.name: Soldiers' Home / Upshur Street line
lines.streets: Soldiers' Home by a route off Georgia Ave; CRF also lists an Upshur St line on old route 74
lines.notes: The original builder isn't named in the sources checked.

lines.name: Columbia Railway – H Street line
lines.streets: Charter route: 15th St & New York Ave NW via New York Ave, K St, Massachusetts Ave and H St NW/NE to 15th St NE
lines.later: Washington Traction & Electric (1899); WRECo (1902); Capital Transit
lines.power: Horse → cable (Mar 9, 1895; the last cable line built in the US) → electric (July 22, 1899)
lines.notes: The last cable car in DC ran July 23, 1899. Revived as the DC Streetcar (2016–2026). Tundria: H St–Benning Rd track closed May 1, 1949.

lines.name: Benning Road – Kenilworth branch
lines.streets: Benning Rd NE east from 15th & H NE across the Anacostia to Kenilworth
lines.notes: Benning Rd car barn built 1941. 1912 map (audit): the branch left Benning Rd just west of Minnesota Ave and ran northeast on its own alignment to Kenilworth; redrawn.

lines.name: Seat Pleasant branch
lines.streets: Benning Rd to Deanwood Junction and Seat Pleasant, MD (connection with the Chesapeake Beach Railway)
lines.notes: Seat Pleasant loop built 1945. 1912 map: ran from Benning Rd up Minnesota Ave and east along Deane Ave (today's Nannie Helen Burroughs Ave) and Dix St to the District line, matching Berman's 1942 map. 1912 map (audit): shared the Kenilworth branch alignment from Benning Rd, then ran straight along Deane Ave (Nannie Helen Burroughs Ave) to the District line; redrawn. CRF dates Seat Pleasant electric service to 1898; WP distinguishes the 1898 Kenilworth line from Seat Pleasant “built 1900”.

lines.name: Anacostia & Potomac River Railroad main line
lines.streets: Along M St from the Maine Ave/M St waterfront to 11th St SE, across the Navy Yard Bridge to Uniontown (Nichols Ave & V St SE), as mapped in 1880. 1888: extensions toward Congressional Cemetery and Center Market; Nichols Ave toward St. Elizabeths (Government Hospital for the Insane)
lines.power: Horse → electric (April 1900, the last horse line in DC)
lines.routes: — (Anacostia service later part of routes 54/A2 corridor)
lines.endtxt: Between 1924 and 1942 (still drawn on the 1924 Rand McNally map; nothing crosses the Anacostia on the 1942 map)
lines.notes: First line to cross the Anacostia River. Probably ended with the 1935 Anacostia conversions, but no source confirms it. Map: the 1888 Center Market branch (G St, 4th St, E St and Canal St SE) is drawn on the 1912 map. 1912 map: the line ran up 11th St SE to G St; there is no track on M St SE, on 7th St SE, or on G St east of 11th St, so those sections are drawn only to 1900 (estimated). 1912 map: the Center Market branch ran up Canal St, west on Maryland Ave, north on 4½ St and along Missouri Ave and B St to 7th St. 1912 map: M St SW between the waterfront and 4½ St was still in use. Initial 1875 terminus was 7th & M St SW; extended to Center Market in 1888.
lines.src: WP; MPD; MAP1880; MAP1910; MAP1924; MAP1942

lines.name: 11th Street line
lines.streets: 11th St: north to Boundary St and south to Water St SW (Belt, 1881); A&PR extended it from F St NW to Florida Ave (1898) and by double track north on 11th St to Lydecker Ave (1902); later to 11th & Monroe NW and through-routed to Anacostia
lines.co: Belt Railway (11th St line, 1881); extended by the A&PR (1898)
lines.later: Washington Traction & Electric; WRECo; Capital Transit; D.C. Transit

lines.name: Capital Railway – Anacostia–Congress Heights
lines.streets: Navy Yard Bridge – Nichols Ave SE to Congress Heights (Upsal St by 1898); later extended past Alabama Ave to Sterling St SE
lines.power: Brown magnetic surface contact (1897, failed) and double-overhead on the bridge → electric
lines.notes: Anacostia's first electric line.

lines.name: Portland Street / Firth Sterling spur
lines.streets: Nichols Ave along Portland St to the Firth Sterling Steel works (now part of Joint Base Anacostia-Bolling)
lines.notes: About one mile of track.

lines.name: Belt Railway loop
lines.streets: Capitol – 1st St SW – Maryland & Virginia Aves SW – 12th St – Ohio Ave – 14th St – O St NW (10 blocks east) – 4th St – G St – 1st St NW; P St NW westbound track (1876)
lines.co: Capitol, North O Street & South Washington Railway (renamed Belt Railway 1893)
lines.endtxt: Absorbed into other routes; end date not stated
lines.notes: 8.5 miles of track. Car barn at 3rd & B (Independence) Sts SW. 1912 map: the loop's south side ran along Maryland Ave SW from 12th St to the Capitol grounds. 1912 map: a branch ran down 11th St SW to the waterfront and along Water St to 7th St. 1912 map (audit): south of New York Ave the loop used New York Ave and 5th St to reach G St, not 4th St.

lines.name: Eckington & Soldiers' Home Railway
lines.streets: Charter: New York Ave from 7th St to 3rd St NE, 3rd St to T St, T St to 4th St, 4th St to Bunker Hill Rd (Michigan Ave). As built: 7th & New York Ave via Boundary St, Eckington Pl, R St, 3rd St and T St NE to the car barn at 4th & T NE
lines.power: DC's first electric line (overhead, Oct 17, 1888) → batteries (1891–93) → horses → compressed air (from Mar 10, 1897; authorized June 10, 1896) → conduit (1899)
lines.notes: 2.5 miles. Also tried the Wheless and Willis magnetic surface-contact systems on North Capitol St. 1912 map: the Eckington loop used both 2nd and 3rd Sts NE between R and T Sts.

lines.name: NE 4th Street branch
lines.streets: 4th St NE north to Michigan Ave; later a Michigan Ave extension to the B&O Metropolitan Branch
lines.notes: CRF gives '1920s' only; end year approximate.

lines.name: Glenwood Cemetery extension
lines.streets: T St, 2nd St and V St NE to Glenwood Cemetery

lines.name: North Capitol Street / Brookland line
lines.streets: North Capitol St to the Soldiers' Home; extended to Brookland (Catholic University) 1899–1900; Brookland/Quincy St loop 1948
lines.notes: 1912 map: continued north on 12th St NE past Monroe St to about Randolph St.

lines.name: G Street extension
lines.streets: 5th St from New York Ave to G St, then G St NW to 15th St (c.1890); 1892–94 downtown loops via 1st St, C St and D St NW, New Jersey Ave, and 5th St, Louisiana Ave, 6th St and B St NW to near 7th St (Center Market)
lines.notes: Authorized 1890.

lines.name: Rhode Island Avenue – College Park line
lines.streets: Rhode Island Ave NE from 4th St NE (connection with Eckington line) to Mount Rainier (1897), Brentwood (1898), Hyattsville and Riverdale (1899), then College Park and Berwyn
lines.co: Maryland & Washington Railway / City & Suburban Railway
lines.endtxt: Sept 7, 1958 (Route 82, one of the first abandoned by D.C. Transit)
lines.notes: Truncated at Beltsville by 1948 and at Berwyn by 1956. Right-of-way partly used by the Rhode Island Ave Trolley Trail.

lines.name: Berwyn – Beltsville – Laurel extension
lines.streets: Riverdale–College Park–Berwyn–Branchville–Beltsville–Contee–Laurel, MD
lines.co: Columbia & Maryland Ry / Berwyn & Laurel Electric RR / Washington, Berwyn & Laurel Electric RR
lines.endtxt: Branchville–Beltsville: July 31, 1949 (CRF); Laurel end not stated
lines.notes: Direct Treasury–Laurel service began 1902.

lines.name: Rock Creek Railway – Connecticut Avenue line
lines.streets: Florida Ave (2 blocks east of Connecticut) – 18th St – Calvert St bridge (1891) – Connecticut Ave to Chevy Chase Circle and Chevy Chase Lake, MD
lines.power: Overhead outside the city; Love conduit inside (1893–99)
lines.endtxt: Sept 16, 1935 (Calvert St bridge to Chevy Chase Lake)
lines.notes: Florida Ave stub (Connecticut Ave–18th St) opened 1890 and was removed 1899. Calvert St bridge completed July 21, 1891. Suburban line opened Sept 16 (Wikipedia) or 18 (NRHP), 1892. Through service to Kensington from 1923. Last cars Sept 15, 1935.

lines.name: U Street line
lines.streets: U St east from 18th St to 7th St NW (1893, Love conduit), later the U St crosstown
lines.later: Capital Traction; Capital Transit; D.C. Transit
lines.notes: Opened Mar 2, 1893 (18th & Florida to 7th St). Love conduit replaced by sliding shoe in 1899. In 1946, routes 90/92 started at the National Zoological Park via Calvert St (Tundria lists 16th St where other sources say 18th St).

lines.name: Florida Avenue / 8th Street extension
lines.streets: U St line extended east on Florida Ave NW/NE to 8th St NE, then south on 8th St NE/SE to the Navy Yard
lines.co: Capital Traction (Act of May 23, 1908; per Tindall and Wikipedia's Capital Traction article; Wikipedia's main article says WRECo)
lines.notes: Rails still buried under 8th St SE. Drawn on the 1910 and 1924 Rand McNally maps. 1912 map: Capital Traction track on F St NE linked Union Station with the 8th St line.

lines.name: New Jersey Avenue line
lines.streets: Florida Ave & New Jersey Ave via New Jersey Ave and Massachusetts Ave to the Union Station plaza (Act of May 23, 1908)

lines.name: Union Station trackage
lines.streets: Delaware Ave NE and Massachusetts Ave NE to Union Station; C St tunnel under Capitol Plaza (1934)
lines.notes: Service began June 24, 1908 (Wikipedia Capital Traction article) or Dec 6, 1908 (NRHP). Capitol Plaza tunnel opened 1934. Map: joint track ran south from Union Station on 1st St NE/SE to Pennsylvania Ave SE (1912 map; route 90 in 1946).

lines.name: Kensington Railway
lines.streets: Chevy Chase Lake north on Connecticut Ave ~0.5 mi, then off-road on a private, winding right-of-way along Silver Creek through Kenilworth / North Chevy Chase to Kensington; extended to Norris Station (1.25 mi) in 1916
lines.later: Kensington Railway; leased to Capital Traction 1923–33
lines.notes: Opened May 30, 1895. Right-of-way became Kensington Parkway. Did not follow Connecticut Ave beyond Chevy Chase Lake; ran on a private ROW along Silver Creek (later Kensington Parkway). The 1916 Norris Station extension was built by the associated Sandy Spring Railway, a separate company with the same owner.

lines.name: Georgetown & Tennallytown line
lines.streets: M St NW up 32nd St and Wisconsin Ave (Georgetown & Rockville Rd) to Tenleytown and Friendship Heights
lines.later: Washington Traction & Electric; WRECo (fully 1926); Capital Transit; D.C. Transit
lines.notes: Opened Apr 25, 1890.

lines.name: Friendship Heights – Bethesda – Rockville line
lines.streets: Wisconsin & Willard Aves (Friendship Heights) along Old Georgetown Rd to Bethesda (Bethesda Park, 3.75 mi, west side between Cedar & Greentree); extended to Rockville in 1900 via Rockville Pike (Alta Vista, Edgemoor, Woodmont, Halpine, Montrose)
lines.co: Tennallytown & Rockville RR (1890); Washington & Rockville Railway (1897)
lines.notes: T&R opened July 4, 1891 to Bethesda Park; foreclosed May 1896. W&R incorporated Sept 9, 1897; tracks to Rockville by 1900, Woodlawn Hotel 1904. 24 trips a day in 1929.

lines.name: Glen Echo Railroad
lines.streets: Wisconsin & Willard Aves west to Conduit Rd (MacArthur Blvd) & Walhonding Rd; 1896 to Glen Echo; ~1898 branch through Somerset to Chevy Chase Circle; Glen Echo to Cabin John reached end of 1898
lines.co: Glen Echo Railroad (1889); Washington & Glen Echo RR (1896)
lines.later: Walhonding–Cabin John section absorbed by Washington & Great Falls (1902)
lines.notes: Opened June 1891. Glen Echo proper opened Apr 1, 1896, but Cabin John Bridge was reached at the end of 1898 (our NPS MPDF source says May 1896, a conflict). A ~1898 branch ran through Somerset to Chevy Chase Circle (through service from Chevy Chase Circle to Cabin John from Dec 1898); the company was absorbed into Washington Traction & Electric in 1899.

lines.name: Cabin John line (Washington & Great Falls)
lines.streets: Falls car barn at 36th & Prospect Sts, west along Prospect St and across the Foundry Branch trestle, then on its own right-of-way along the south side of the Georgetown Reservoir and through the Palisades (today's Palisades Trolley Trail), past Chain Bridge and north through Brookmont to Glen Echo Park, then on the old Glen Echo Railroad right-of-way to a turning loop at the east end of the Cabin John Bridge
lines.notes: Chartered July 29, 1892. Reached the MD line Sept 28, 1895 and Cabin John 1897; double-tracked by 1899. Foundry Branch trestle survives. Route checked against the 1897 company map, the 1907 Baist atlas and the 1951 USGS topographic map: the line ran through Brookmont (not along MacArthur Blvd past the Dalecarlia plant) and ended at a loop by the Cabin John Bridge, not in Cabin John village. Alignment traced from OpenStreetMap's mapped trolley right-of-way, the Foundry Branch trestle and the Cabin John loop. 1912 map: from the car barn the line ran west along the bluff below Georgetown University and curved north to the Foundry Branch trestle.
lines.src: WP; WPMD; MPD; CRF; DDOT Palisades Trolley Trail Historic Resources Report (2019); USGS 1951 topo

lines.name: West Washington & Great Falls Electric Railway
lines.streets: Junction with the Tennallytown & Rockville at Wisconsin Ave, west to Glen Echo, largely along today's Bradley Blvd
lines.co: West Washington & Great Falls Electric Railway
lines.notes: Founded Nov 1, 1895. Distinct from the Glen Echo Railroad’s Chevy Chase branch; acquired by the Washington & Great Falls Electric Railway July 1, 1896.
lines.unmapped: Route along Bradley Blvd and toward Glen Echo not confirmed; removed from the map.

lines.name: Brightwood Ry – Petworth / Kenyon St branch
lines.streets: Rock Creek Church Rd & Richmond St (Petworth) west on Richmond St to Georgia Ave; south on Georgia Ave to Marshall St; west on Marshall St to Kenyon Ave; Kenyon to 14th St
lines.endtxt: Ordered vacated between 7th and 14th Sts (act c.1893–95)
lines.notes: Authorized Feb 27, 1893. A later act ordered the Kenyon and Marshall St track and poles removed within a month unless converted to underground power. End year approximate. Route per the authorizing act of Feb 27, 1893 (27 Stat. 490): junction at Rock Creek Church Rd & Richmond St (Petworth), westerly on Richmond St to Brightwood Ave (Georgia Ave), southerly to Marshall St, westerly on Marshall St to Kenyon Ave, then to 14th St.

lines.name: City & Suburban – Stanton Square / C & D St NE loop
lines.streets: From New Jersey Ave east on C St around Stanton Square, then C and D Sts NE to a turn at 13th St; Stanton Square track moved to the north side c.1902–03
lines.co: Eckington & Soldiers' Home Railway (renamed City & Suburban Railway of Washington, 1898)
lines.notes: Authorized 1892, route rewritten Aug 23, 1894. Drawn on the 1910 and 1924 Rand McNally maps and on the 1942 and 1958 system maps. In 1946, route 42 ran out via Massachusetts Ave, Maryland Ave and D St to 13th St, returning via C and 6th Sts (Tundria). The 1912 map colors this loop as WRECo. 1912 map: track on Massachusetts Ave NE linked Union Station with Stanton Square (route 42 used it in 1946). 1912 map: cars reached Stanton Square from Union Station by Massachusetts Ave, ran along the square's north side and down 6th St to C St; C St west of the square is not shown in 1912, so it is drawn only to 1908 (estimated). The Stanton Square track is documented under the City & Suburban Railway of Washington: the joint resolution of March 3, 1899 (30 Stat. 1391) authorized C&S to relocate its Stanton Square track. Start may be closer to 1897–98; no horsecar phase (electric throughout).
lines.src: LAWS; MAP1910; MAP1924; MAP1942; MAP1958; TUN; MAP1912

lines.name: West End loops / Potomac Park terminal
lines.streets: First loops (1901): out Pennsylvania Ave, south on 25th St to G St, and south on 26th St to F St, returning east on G and F Sts to 17th St (a short G St link joined 25th and 26th Sts). Second loop (approved Dec 7, 1916): 18th and 19th Sts south to Virginia Ave. Routes 80/82 ended here as 'Potomac Park' / 'Virginia Ave' (out 18th St, back 19th St)
lines.endtxt: Sept 7, 1958 (routes 80 and 82 converted; still on Wagner's Aug 1958 map)
lines.notes: The 1910 Rand McNally map shows only the 1901 loops; the 1924 map shows track reaching Virginia Ave. The 18th St extension into Potomac Park was the District Commissioners' top recommendation in 1912. Identifying the Potomac Park terminal with the 1916 loop is an inference from the maps. 1912 map: West End loops on 25th and 26th Sts, G and F Sts; 26th St south of H St no longer exists, so that stretch is drawn straight.
lines.src: WP-PennAve; TIN; MAP1910; MAP1924; MAP1942; TUN; MAP1958; MAP1912

lines.name: McLean Gardens loop
lines.streets: Turning loop off Wisconsin Ave at McLean Gardens
lines.notes: Shown on Wagner's Aug 1958 trackage map; opening date not found. End date inferred from the route 30 conversion.

lines.name: Louisiana Ave trackage (route 20 to Union Station)
lines.streets: From Pennsylvania Ave via 1st St NW and Louisiana Ave toward Union Station
lines.notes: Only source for the closing date is Tundria's list of 1946–58 abandonments. Opening date not found.

lines.name: Washington & Great Falls Railway & Power Co.
lines.streets: Wisconsin Ave & Bradley Lane along what is now Bradley Blvd to Great Falls, MD (10.66 mi)
lines.co: Washington & Great Falls Railway & Power Co. (operated by WRECo)
lines.notes: The only line that actually reached Great Falls.

lines.name: Forest Glen line
lines.streets: Georgia & Eastern Aves (end of Brightwood line) along Georgia Ave and Seminary Rd to the National Park Seminary, Forest Glen (2.9 mi)
lines.notes: Opened Nov 25, 1897. CRF gives electric 1895.

lines.name: 'Dinky Line' – Takoma to Sligo
lines.streets: 4th & Butternut Sts NW via 4th St, Aspen St and Laurel St into Takoma Park to Wildwood / Glen Sligo Hotel; Carroll Ave extension to the Sanitarium (1918)
lines.power: Electric (1897) → abandoned c.1903–07 → gasoline cars (May 30, 1910) → storage battery → electric
lines.notes: Leased by Capital Traction May 2, 1918 (Wikipedia main article says owned 1916). The original resort line closed around 1904; the tracks were removed and later rebuilt.

lines.name: Kennedy Street / 3rd Street – Takoma line
lines.streets: 3rd St NW and Kennedy St NW to 14th St & Colorado Ave (connection with 14th St line)
lines.notes: Built between 1903 and 1917 (Wikipedia); CRF dates it 1910. Capital Traction also operated this line as route 58 (the "14th St–Takoma" service) from the 14th St & Colorado Ave connection. This entry absorbed the former separate L44 "14th St–Takoma" line, which had no track of its own (the "via Eastern Ave" routing was unsupported). Operated 1910–14 by the Baltimore & Washington Transit Co. (gasoline cars from May 30, 1910; storage-battery from 1911); renamed the Washington & Maryland Railway on March 4, 1914, which electrified the line that year (CRF’s “elec 1910” marks route establishment). CRF dates abandonment April 1936; WP and Historic Takoma say 1937.

lines.name: East Washington Heights Traction
lines.streets: Pennsylvania Ave SE from the Capitol to Barney Circle (1903), across the bridge to Randle Highlands at 27th St SE (1908), past 33rd St SE (1917)
lines.notes: Two streetcars, about one mile of track. The 1910 Rand McNally map shows the line crossing the Pennsylvania Ave bridge (the 1908 extension). The 1924 map may still show it because of plate lag. The Pennsylvania Ave bridge crossing opened in 1905 (terminating at Minnesota Ave SE); 1908 was the extension to 27th St SE. No horsecar phase is attested (an electric "traction" company), so the 1903–1905 horse segment is uncertain.

lines.name: Bladensburg Road line
lines.streets: 15th & H Sts NE along Bladensburg Rd to Bladensburg (1910); battery-car extension to Berwyn Heights (1912)
lines.power: Electric in DC; storage-battery cars in MD
lines.notes: MD charter Feb 13, 1905; DC entry Feb 18, 1907. 2.89 mi in DC and 5.55 mi in MD. Not drawn on either the 1910 or the 1924 Rand McNally map. WRECo formally operated the line from Oct 1913 (through route from the 15th & H St NE loop to Bladensburg); the franchise was sold in 1915 and WRECo control ended.

lines.name: Massachusetts Avenue line
lines.streets: Massachusetts Ave NW
lines.unmapped: Exact route on Massachusetts Ave not identified.

lines.name: LeDroit Park line
lines.streets: Belt Railway extension (1896): 4th & O NW north on 4th St to Florida Ave, then Harewood, Elm, Linden and Pomeroy Sts to 7th St, LeDroit Park; through-routed to the wharves by Washington Traction
lines.notes: Drawn on the 1924 Rand McNally map (loop near Howard University and the ballpark). Map: ran into LeDroit Park via 3rd St, Elm St, 4th St and V St to Georgia Ave (1912 map). 1912 map: the LeDroit Park line reached Georgia Ave along W St. The LeDroit Park branch itself opened in 1896 (start 1875 reflects the parent Belt Railway line it ran over).

lines.name: Key Bridge – Rosslyn line
lines.streets: M St across the Francis Scott Key Bridge to the Rosslyn loop and W&OD terminal
lines.endtxt: Aug 26, 1956 (Wikipedia, CRF) or Dec 24, 1948 (Tundria): unresolved conflict
lines.notes: Replaced W&OD service over the old Aqueduct Bridge. The Rosslyn loop stood at Rosslyn Circle at the Virginia foot of Key Bridge (rebuilt as a circle in 1940), beside the W&OD Rosslyn terminal.

lines.name: 14th St – U St – 11th St route
lines.streets: Capital Transit 1936 through-route combining 14th St, U St and 11th St trackage
lines.unmapped: Through-route over existing 14th St, U St and 11th St track.

lines.name: Bureau of Engraving loop / Southwest government trackage
lines.streets: 14th St SW to the Bureau of Engraving (service since at least 1895); underground loop at 14th & C Sts SW (1942); new track 1939–41 to government buildings southwest of the Mall
lines.notes: Loop is now part of a parking and storage structure under 14th St SW.

lines.name: Washington, Alexandria & Mount Vernon line
lines.streets: Mount Vernon – Alexandria – Arlington Junction – Long Bridge (Highway Bridge from Feb 12, 1906) – DC. DC route 1896: 14th & B via B St, 13½ St and E St to 14th St on Belt tracks. From 1902: 12th & D, 12th St, C St, 14th St
lines.co: Washington, Alexandria & Mount Vernon Electric Railway
lines.notes: Alexandria–Mount Vernon service began 1892. The 1902 DC terminal was at 1204 Pennsylvania Ave NW (12th–13th Sts); it moved to 12th & D in 1905 to make way for the new City Hall. The Alexandria–Mount Vernon segment was abandoned in early 1930 (announced Feb 20, 1930).

lines.name: Rosslyn branch (East Arlington)
lines.streets: Arlington Junction – Mt. Vernon Junction – along Arlington Ridge Rd – Rosslyn (Aqueduct Bridge)
lines.co: Washington, Alexandria & Mount Vernon Electric Railway
lines.notes: Opened May 22, 1896.

lines.name: Nauck (Fort Myer) line
lines.streets: Rosslyn south through Fort Myer (N. Lynn St, N. Meade St, McNair Rd) to Nauck near Four Mile Run
lines.notes: Electrification year not documented; drawn as electric from 1896, when the company opened its electric Fairfax line. Through service into DC ended Jan 17, 1932; streetcars were replaced by auto-railers in 1936 and the last auto-railer ran Sept 9, 1939. Electrification was late 1895 (not 1896) per Merriken, after the 1893 foreclosure shutdown.

lines.name: Fairfax line
lines.streets: Rosslyn / DC via Clarendon, Ballston, Falls Church, Dunn Loring, Vienna and Oakton to the Fairfax County Courthouse
lines.endtxt: DC service ended Jan 17, 1932; company bankrupt 1939
lines.notes: Reached Falls Church 1897 and Fairfax Nov 28, 1904. Oakton station is on the NRHP. Through DC service ended Jan 17, 1932 and the Clarendon–Arlington Junction rail was abandoned Aug 1, 1932, but Clarendon–Falls Church–Fairfax rail ran until Sept 9, 1939.

lines.name: North Arlington branch
lines.streets: Rosslyn / DC (transfer at Georgetown / Aqueduct Bridge) – Clarendon – Ballston – Falls Church; Rosslyn – N. Lynn St – Fairfax Dr – Clarendon Blvd
lines.notes: Roughly follows today's Orange/Silver Metro alignment. Track Rosslyn–Clarendon–Ballston–Falls Church was laid and operated electric in 1896, when the company was renamed the Washington, Arlington & Falls Church Railway.

lines.name: South Arlington branch (Clarendon Cutoff)
lines.streets: Clarendon southeast along Washington Blvd to Mt. Vernon Junction and Arlington Junction

lines.name: Great Falls & Old Dominion (W&OD Great Falls Division) into Georgetown
lines.streets: Rosslyn (VA, W&OD Rosslyn Terminal) – northwest along the north side of Lee Highway through Cherrydale – own right-of-way (now Old Dominion Dr / SR-309) via McLean to Great Falls Park; across the Potomac on the Aqueduct Bridge to a station at 36th St south of Prospect St (next to the Georgetown Car Barn)
lines.endtxt: 1923 (replaced by Capital Traction's Key Bridge service)
lines.notes: Authorized Jan 29, 1903; trial runs from Georgetown Mar 1906; scheduled service July 3, 1906. 1923 marks the end of the Georgetown (DC) operation when the Aqueduct Bridge closed for the Key Bridge (opened Jan 1923); the W&OD Great Falls Division itself (Rosslyn–Great Falls) continued until abandoned in June 1934.

lines.name: Washington, Baltimore & Annapolis Electric Railway
lines.streets: Terminal at 15th & H Sts NE, over Benning Rd streetcar tracks and the Benning Rd bridge to Deanwood, then its own line to Baltimore and Annapolis
lines.notes: Main access to Suburban Gardens amusement park.

events.t: Congress incorporates the Washington & Georgetown Railroad, authorizing three horsecar lines.
First car runs on Pennsylvania Ave from the Capitol to the White House / State Dept.
Line extended west to Washington Circle.
Line extended to Georgetown (Bridge & High Sts, now M St & Wisconsin Ave).
Line extended east to the Navy Yard gate via A St S, Pennsylvania Ave and 8th St SE; full Georgetown–Navy Yard service begins.
7th Street line opens from N St NW to the Potomac River.
14th St branch opens (White House – New York Ave – 14th St to Florida Ave); W&G article says 'by 1870'.
Extended north to Boundary St (Florida Ave).
Law permits the line to continue north of Boundary St.
Metropolitan Railroad chartered.
First lines complete: Capitol to 14th & I Sts NW, and H St NW from Massachusetts Ave to 17th St.
Two-horse cars replaced by one-horse cars.
Amendment authorizes 4½ St line from Missouri Ave to P St SW (Arsenal).
Extension authorized via A St, 1st St and East Capitol St to 9th St east.
Connecticut Avenue & Park Railway chartered.
Columbia Railway chartered: 15th & New York Ave via New York Ave, K St, Massachusetts Ave and H St to 15th St NE.
9th Street line opens from M St NW, joining the Georgia Ave line.
Union Railroad chartered for a route to Georgetown via Connecticut Ave and P St.
Metropolitan absorbs the Union Railroad without congressional authority.
Boundary & Silver Spring Railway chartered (Tindall says the charter was later forfeited).
Single track with turnouts doubled.
A&PR incorporated under the 1870 general incorporation law (Wikipedia: chartered May 5, 1870).
Horsecars begin on Connecticut Ave, but only as far north as P St; tracks north of P St paved over.
Metropolitan builds on Florida Ave and Georgia Ave to Rock Creek Church Rd.
Absorbed by the Metropolitan.
Tracks moved off Capitol Grounds to 1st St W and B St S; Rock Creek crossing moved from the Pennsylvania Ave bridge to the M St bridge via 26th St.
Authorized along Water St and P St SW to the Arsenal gate, sharing A&PR tracks.
B&O depot branch relocated to 1st St W and C St N, ending at New Jersey Ave.
Congress sanctions the Anacostia & Potomac River Railroad.
Line opens from the Arsenal via M St SW/SE and 11th St SE across the Navy Yard Bridge to Nichols Ave & V St SE.
Belt Railway incorporated; loop via 1st St SW, Maryland & Virginia Aves, 12th St, Ohio Ave, 14th St, O St, 4th St, G St and 1st St NW.
P St NW track added for westbound cars.
Balance of the Georgetown / P Street route completed.
Belt Railway extends its 11th St line north to Boundary St and south to Water St SW.
Buried tracks between P St and Florida Ave reopened as a shuttle after residents' petition.
Line built down 4th St NW/SW to P St SW, partly via unauthorized tracks on Missouri Ave, 6th St and B St.
Brightwood Railway chartered to electrify and extend to the District line.
Extensions to Congressional Cemetery (11th & G Sts SE) and past Garfield Park to Center Market; Nichols Ave extended toward Alabama Ave.
Eckington & Soldiers' Home Railway chartered.
DC's first electric streetcar opens (overhead trolley).
Opens: 4th St NE north to Michigan Ave.
Rock Creek Railway incorporated by the Chevy Chase Land Co. group.
Georgetown & Tennallytown Railway chartered.
Judson pneumatic system tried from Florida Ave to Rock Creek Church Rd; fails in icing.
Opens: T St, 2nd St and V St NE to Glenwood Cemetery.
DC's first cable line opens on 7th St, Arsenal to Florida Ave (3.5 mi); Wikipedia gives Apr 12, NRHP May 12.
Metropolitan sells the line to the Brightwood Railway.
Wheless and later Willis magnetic surface-contact systems tried on North Capitol St.
First quarter-mile opens on Florida Ave between Connecticut Ave and 18th St (Love conduit).
Rock Creek route set: Florida Ave, 18th St, the Calvert St bridge and Connecticut Ave, plus U St to 14th St.
Service opens from M St up 32nd St and Wisconsin Ave to Tenleytown, later to Wisconsin & Willard Aves.
Storage-battery cars tried between 5th & New York Ave and 15th & G Sts.
Opens: 5th St from New York Ave to G St, then G St NW to 15th St (c.1890).
Calvert St iron truss bridge over Rock Creek completed; bridges transferred to DC July 20.
Tennallytown & Rockville opens 3.75 mi along Old Georgetown Rd to Bethesda Park.
Glen Echo Railroad opens west from Wisconsin & Willard to Conduit & Walhonding Rds.
Entire W&G system running on cable; two cables haul cars between the Navy Yard and Georgetown.
Extended up the hill to Mount Pleasant St (Park Rd); Mount Pleasant car barn built.
Congress orders overhead electric operation and completion of the line.
Brightwood allowed overhead wires; ordered to reach the District line within 12 months and build the Takoma branch via 5th and Umatilla Sts.
Maryland & Washington Railway chartered: Rhode Island Ave from 4th St NE to the District line.
Six-mile extension up Connecticut Ave to Chevy Chase Lake opens; first DC company to run in Maryland.
Washington & Great Falls Electric Railway chartered (Aqueduct Bridge to Cabin John Creek).
Opens: Rosslyn south through Fort Myer (N. Lynn St, N. Meade St, McNair Rd) to Nauck near Four Mile Run.
Spur opens via Butternut (Umatilla) St to 4th St, Takoma Park.
Opens: Soldiers' Home by a route off Georgia Ave.
Renamed Belt Railway Company.
U St extension from 18th & Florida east to 7th St NW opens.
Double-tracked; through Georgetown–Bethesda Park service begins.
Brightwood Ry authorized to build an overhead-trolley branch via Richmond, Marshall and Kenyon Sts from Petworth to 14th St.
Authorized to extend on M St to the Aqueduct Bridge and build a 'Union Station' (Georgetown Car Barn).
Streetcar service ends.
Brightwood ordered to vacate the Kenyon and Marshall St track between 7th and 14th Sts within a month.
Eckington downtown loop authorized: G St, 1st St and C St NW, then around Stanton Square and along C and D Sts NE (built to 13th St).
WA&MV authorized to enter DC.
WA&MV authorized to run into DC via B St, 13½ St and E St to 14th St, then over Belt tracks to the Potomac.
First underground-conduit electric operation in the Western Hemisphere installed on the 9th St line.
Act authorizes a single-track underground-electric loop on P, 36th, Prospect and 35th Sts in Georgetown.
4½ Street car barn and shops built at 4th & P Sts SW.
Cable operation begins (last cable line built in the US).
Capital Railway chartered.
Opens: Chevy Chase Lake north along Connecticut Ave to University Blvd, Kensington.
Tracks reach the Maryland line; service begins.
Opens: 14th St SW to the Bureau of Engraving (service since at least 1895).
West Washington & Great Falls Electric Railway founded: Wisconsin Ave junction west toward Glen Echo along today's Bradley Blvd.
Metropolitan system converted to underground electric.
Extended along East Capitol St to 15th St; East Capitol St car barn built.
Capital Ry authorized to cross the Navy Yard bridge; built from the bridge along Nichols Ave to Congress Heights.
Compressed-air motors tried; failure sends company into receivership.
Sold at foreclosure; Bethesda Park wrecked by hurricane.
Service reaches Glen Echo, then Cabin John a month later; Chevy Chase Circle branch built.
Falls car barn built at 38th & Prospect Sts.
Baltimore & Washington Transit incorporated; authorized to enter DC to meet the Brightwood spur.
Belt authorized to build north on 4th St from O St across Florida Ave into LeDroit Park (Harewood, Elm, Linden, Pomeroy Sts to 7th St).
Acquired by the Washington & Great Falls Electric Railway.
Tracks completed; DC route from 14th & B via B St, 13½ St and E St to 14th St and the Long Bridge on Belt tracks.
Opens: Arlington Junction – Mt. Vernon Junction – along Arlington Ridge Rd – Rosslyn (Aqueduct Bridge).
Opens: Rosslyn / DC via Clarendon, Ballston, Falls Church, Dunn Loring, Vienna and Oakton to the Fairfax County Courthouse.
Georgetown Car Barn / Union Depot at 36th & M opens with DC's only cable loop.
Cable powerhouse at 14th & E NW burns; cars revert to horses.
Act authorizes extension on Columbia Rd and Mount Pleasant Rd to Park Rd.
Brown magnetic surface-contact system laid from 8th & M SE to the Navy Yard Bridge; removal approved Jan 20, 1899.
Line reaches Mount Rainier.
Washington & Rockville Electric Railway incorporated.
Line reaches Glen Echo and Cabin John.
Opens: Georgia & Eastern Aves (end of Brightwood line) along Georgia Ave and Seminary Rd to the National Park Seminary, Forest Glen (2.9 mi).
Line built from 4th & Butternut via 4th St, Aspen and Laurel Sts to Wildwood / Glen Sligo.
Pennsylvania Ave division electrified by underground conduit (west of the Capitol from Mar 20).
7th Street branch electrified (conduit).
14th Street line electrified after the 1897 powerhouse fire.
Brightwood ordered to switch to underground electric.
Benning Rd extension with overhead wires to Kenilworth.
Columbia authorized to cross the Anacostia on a wooden trestle and run via Race Course Rd and the Anacostia road to the District's eastern corner.
A&PR extends the 11th St line from F St NW to Florida Ave.
Line reaches Congress Heights (Upsal St) via Nichols Ave.
Absorbed by the A&PR; conduit electric installed 1899.
Buys the Maryland & Washington Railway and renames itself the City & Suburban Railway of Washington.
Eckington car barn and 30 cars burn; new barn built 1899.
Reaches Brentwood (1898), then Hyattsville and Riverdale (1899).
East Washington Heights Traction chartered.
Switch to electric; last DC cable car runs the next day.
Bought by the A&PR.
North Capitol service extended to Brookland / Catholic University.
Florida Ave spur between 18th St and Connecticut Ave removed; transfer point moved to the Calvert St loop.
Love conduit replaced by standard sliding-shoe conduit.
Double-tracked; wooden trestles replaced with steel.
Capital Traction authorized to double-track Pennsylvania Ave SE from 8th to 15th St E with a loop around square 1078.
Service to Mount Pleasant begins.
Act authorizes extension east on Columbia Rd to old 16th St (Mount Pleasant St) and north to Park St.
Seat Pleasant branch connects with the Chesapeake Beach Railway.
Last horsecar company in DC switches to electric.
Tracks completed from Bethesda Park to Courthouse Square, Rockville; town withholds permission until the hotel extension is built.
West End loop opens: 17th St, G St, 25th/26th Sts and F St.
Pennsylvania Ave SE extended from 8th St to 17th St SE (later Barney Circle).
First West End loop opens (17th, G, 25th/26th and F Sts).
Metropolitan absorbed into WRECo.
A&PR required to extend the 11th St line by double track north from Florida Ave to Lydecker Ave.
Direct Treasury–Laurel service begins (Washington, Berwyn & Laurel).
Operations end except Walhonding Rd–Cabin John section, absorbed by the W&GF.
DC route changed to start at 12th & D; south on 12th, west on C, south on 14th.
City & Suburban required to double-track North Capitol St from T St to Michigan Ave (overhead trolley until 1904 or paving).
Takoma Park takes over the lease; line derelict and rails removed.
Reaches Barney Circle (1903), then across the bridge to Randle Highlands (1908).
Stanton Square track moved from the south to the north side of the square.
Great Falls & Old Dominion authorized to enter DC over the Aqueduct Bridge.
Line reaches the Woodlawn Hotel, Rockville.
Washington, Spa Spring & Gretta chartered in Maryland; DC entry authorized Feb 18, 1907 and Mar 3, 1909.
Extended from Park Rd to Decatur St car barn and Colorado Ave.
Cars move from the Long Bridge to the new Highway Bridge.
Opens: Clarendon – Clarendon Blvd / Fairfax Dr / N. Lynn St – Rosslyn.
Trial runs from Georgetown in March; scheduled service to Great Falls, VA begins July 3.
Opens: Clarendon southeast along Washington Blvd to Mt. Vernon Junction and Arlington Junction.
Branch extended east on C St and northeast on Delaware Ave to Union Station.
Capital Traction authorized to build from 7th & Florida east on Florida Ave and south on 8th St to Pennsylvania Ave, plus F St NE and Union Station connections.
New Jersey Ave and Massachusetts Ave line to the Union Station plaza authorized.
Streetcar service to Union Station begins (Wikipedia / NRHP).
Tenallytown car barn at 5230 Wisconsin Ave replaces the 1890 barn at Calvert St.
Extension along 3rd St and Kennedy St to 14th & Colorado authorized.
Opens: Massachusetts Ave NW.
Opens: Terminal at 15th & H Sts NE, over Benning Rd streetcar tracks and the Benning Rd bridge to Deanwood, then its own line to Baltimore and Annapolis.
Brightwood car house built at 5929 Georgia Ave.
Line reopened with gasoline cars.
Through service begins over existing track.
Service begins from 15th & H NE out Bladensburg Rd.
Merged with the WA&FC into the Washington-Virginia Railway.
Controlling stock bought by WRECo.
Opens: Nichols Ave along Portland St to the Firth Sterling Steel works (now part of Joint Base Anacostia-Bolling).
Battery-car extension to Berwyn Heights; renamed Washington Interurban Railway (Oct 1912).
Washington & Great Falls Railway & Power Co. opens to Great Falls, MD.
Renamed Washington & Maryland Railway.
Cars return to the rebuilt Pennsylvania Ave bridge over Rock Creek (eastbound July 7, westbound July 15).
Second West End loop approved via 18th and 19th Sts to Virginia Ave.
Second West End loop approved via 18th and 19th Sts to Virginia Ave (later the Potomac Park terminal of routes 80/82).
Leased by Capital Traction; Carroll Ave extension to the Sanitarium.
Service ends; tracks removed 1926.
Streetcar service ends (Rosslyn–Mt. Vernon Jct discontinued May 1921).
Streetcar service ends.
Through service to Kensington via the Kensington Railway.
Converted to buses; the first streetcar-to-bus conversion in DC.
Converted to buses.
Capital Traction begins running across the new Key Bridge to a Rosslyn loop.
W&OD leaves Georgetown when the Aqueduct Bridge closes; terminal moved to Rosslyn.
Streetcar service ends; replaced by Bus.
Streetcar service ends; replaced by Bus G8.
Streetcar service ends; replaced by Bus N4.
WRECo buys remaining G&T stock.
Takoma–Old Bladensburg service converted to buses.
Last Virginia streetcar leaves 12th & D Sts NW.
Streetcar service ends.
Streetcar service ends (DC service ended Jan 17, 1932; company bankrupt 1939); replaced by Arlington & Fairfax Motor Transportation Co..
Streetcar service ends.
After the merger, WRECo's parallel Georgetown line is abandoned; Cabin John and Tenleytown cars reroute via Pennsylvania Ave.
Converted to buses (NRHP: 1933 with 9th St rebuilding; Ghosts of DC: 1936).
P Street line (Dupont Circle–Wisconsin Ave) converted to buses.
Anacostia–Congress Heights converted to buses (CRF / Wikipedia dates).
Last streetcars on the Chevy Chase line; buses from Sept 16.
Streetcar service ends.
Rockville service ends; Wisconsin & Western terminal opens.
Streetcar service ends.
Kennedy St / 3rd St service converted to buses.
Streetcar service ends (April 1936 (CRF); Wikipedia says the Takoma line converted by 1937); replaced by Bus K8.
Through service begins over existing track.
First PCC cars enter service on 14th St.
Streetcar service ends.
Underground loop terminal opens at 14th & C Sts SW under the Bureau of Engraving.
Opens: Turning loop off Wisconsin Ave at McLean Gardens.
Seat Pleasant loop built for PCC cars.
Buses replace streetcars Kenilworth–Seat Pleasant.
Line truncated at Beltsville; then at Berwyn by 1956.
Tundria dates the end of streetcars across Key Bridge to Rosslyn here (conflicts with Aug 26, 1956 in Wikipedia and CRF).
Dupont Circle streetcar underpass opens (N St to R St).
Route 10 (H St–Benning) converted to buses.
Track closed on New York Ave, Mount Vernon Sq, H St, Benning Rd and the Benning Rd bridge to Kenilworth and Capitol Heights (routes 10, 12).
Louisiana Ave track closed (route 20).
Last streetcar across Key Bridge; end of streetcars in Virginia.
Route 80 (Rosslyn–Brookland) converted to buses.
Streetcar service ends.
Route 82 (Potomac Park–Branchville) converted to buses.
Routes 80 and 82 converted to buses; Potomac Park loop out of service.
Route 30 (Friendship Heights–Barney Circle) converted to buses.
Georgia Ave–7th St streetcars (routes 70/72/74) converted to buses; 7th Street barn closed.
Streetcar service ends; replaced by Bus 60.
Route 20 converted to buses.
Streetcar service ends (Probably Jan 3, 1960 with route 30 (inferred)); replaced by Buses.
F St/D St service (route 42) converted to buses.
Mount Pleasant line (routes 40/42) converted to buses.
11th Street line (route 60) converted to buses.
Route 42 (Mount Pleasant–13th & C/D NE) converted to buses; the Stanton Square / C & D St NE loop closes.
Tracks east of 14th St last used (routes 54 and 90).
Routes 50 and 54 end; last scheduled car leaves 14th & Colorado at 2:17 am.
East Capitol line (route 40/96) ends with the system.
Streetcar service ends; replaced by Discontinued.
Streetcar service ends; replaced by Bus 50s.
